answer: No, you don't need a paper lien release. Texas uses electronic titles, so your lender sends the lien release to the state electronically, and we transfer the title electronically at your appointment. If the bank still shows as lienholder, the lien hasn't been released yet, so ask your lender to release it. If that doesn't work, you can sign the lien release request, form NW-LRL-1, and we'll contact the lender for you. That can add 1 to 2 weeks, but we can still make you an offer and book your appointment while you wait.
